speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing difficulties conceiving and discomfort during sexual activity. To begin our evaluation, has this pain occurred before or after you started trying to conceive, and does it happen with every attempt to have intercourse?

speaker: Patient
text: 30-year-old female. The patient and her husband have been trying to conceive for 15 months without success. They are sexually active at least twice a week. The husband occasionally has difficulties maintaining an erection. The patient reports discomfort and pelvic floor muscle tension during attempted vaginal penetration. Diagnosed with body dysmorphic disorder three years ago. No family history of serious illness. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. No medications.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Vaginismus (likely secondary to body dysmorphic disorder) contributing to secondary infertility.

Based on your history of pelvic floor tension and difficulty with penetration, I need to confirm if this pain prevents complete insertion or causes spasms immediately before intercourse. Have you experienced any bleeding or injury to the vaginal opening during these attempts?
